classification.difficultyReason: The named triangles scaffold the SSS proof; the student must then select corresponding angles and use converse alternate-angle reasoning to establish both pairs of parallel sides.

content.prompt: All sides of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ below are equal.

spec.description: Unfilled quadrilateral with vertical AD and BC, AB and DC rising to the right, and one equality tick on each side. Ordinary source blue outlines are changed to house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=CD=DA. No diagonal, parallel arrows or angle markings are supplied. Coordinates define illustrative geometry, not numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Vertex labels and four equality ticks are permanent givens. No solution construction is shown.

answer.worked:
Join $BD$. In $\triangle ADB$ and $\triangle CBD$:
$$\begin{aligned}AD&=CB&&\text{(given)}\\AB&=CD&&\text{(given)}\\DB&=BD&&\text{(common side).}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle ADB\equiv\triangle CBD$ by SSS.

inlines.text: You have now proved that every rhombus is a parallelogram.

answer.short:
$AB\parallel DC$ and $AD\parallel BC$, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

Matching angles of the congruent triangles give equal alternate angles for each pair of opposite sides.
answer.worked:
From part a, $\angle ABD=\angle CDB$ (matching angles of congruent triangles). These are alternate angles on transversal $BD$, so $AB\parallel DC$.

Also, $\angle ADB=\angle CBD$ (matching angles of congruent triangles). These are alternate angles on transversal $BD$, so $AD\parallel BC$.

Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel. Therefore $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.
